paraphrase: The gods ask Prajāpati who Sītā is; she is the primordial nature (mūlaprakṛti), called praṇava-prakṛti, the power of Rāma; the syllables of her name are explained.

checks.note: E-text sections 1-2: the gods ask Prajāpati who Sītā is; she is mūlaprakṛti, the power of Rāma, and the syllables of her name are explained.

paraphrase: She has three forms and three powers: will (as Śrī, Bhū and Nīlā), action (from nāda, bindu, Oṃ and the Vedas) and direct manifestation; she is the power of yoga, enjoyment and heroism.

checks.note: The e-text numbers the Sītā in 8 prose sections, so there is no section 9 or 10. The three powers are in sections 3-8: icchāśakti as Śrī, Bhū and Nīlā in section 3, then kriyāśakti and sākṣācchakti, with yogaśakti and bhogaśakti in section 7 and vīraśakti in section 8.
